note: Order is registration order, which is the order the provider sees. definitions_for_provider() does not sort (tools/__init__.py:484).

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a text file from the workspace.

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Write (or overwrite) a text file in the workspace. Use a workspace-relative path (e.g. 'wiki/note.md'). The 'content' parameter must be the full file text — never null or empty unless you intend a blank file.

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description: Replace text in a workspace file.

tools.name: glob_search
tools.description: Search files by glob within the workspace.

tools.name: grep_search
tools.description: Search file contents with ripgrep.

tools.name: list_directory
tools.description: List files and subdirectories in a workspace directory. Returns each entry's name, type (file/dir), and size for files.

path.description: Directory path relative to workspace root. Defaults to workspace root.

tools.name: read_files
tools.description: Read multiple text files in one call. Returns a JSON array; each entry is either {path, content, total_lines} on success or {path, error} on failure. Up to 10 paths per call. Use this instead of N sequential read_file calls when you need to compare or correlate content across files.

paths.description: Workspace-relative or absolute paths to read.

offset.description: Optional 1-based start line, applied to each file.

tools.name: file_outline
tools.description: Return a structural outline of a Python file (classes, methods, functions, top-level imports) with line numbers. Much cheaper than read_file when you only need to locate a symbol. Non-Python files return an error suggesting read_file.

tools.name: apply_patch
tools.description:
Apply a multi-file patch in one call: create, delete, move/rename, and edit any number of files atomically (if any operation fails, nothing is written).

Format:
*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: <path>
+line1
+line2
*** Update File: <path>
*** Move to: <new path>          (optional — renames while editing)
@@ <optional context, e.g. a function name>
 <unchanged context line, space-prefixed>
-<line to remove>
+<line to add>
*** End of File                  (optional — anchors the hunk at end of file)
*** Delete File: <path>
*** End Patch

Hunks must match the file's CURRENT content exactly (context + removed lines, contiguous). Prefer this over edit_file when a change spans multiple files or needs to create/delete/rename in the same operation; use edit_file for a single in-place string replacement.

patch.description: The full patch text, from *** Begin Patch to *** End Patch.

tools.name: bash
tools.description:
Execute a shell command in the workspace.
- Each call gets a fresh shell: no cd, no exported variable, and no activated virtualenv survives to the next call. Use working_directory instead of `cd`, and combine dependent steps in one command.
- On Windows commands run through cmd.exe, not bash. Prefer portable invocations (`python -m ...`) over shell-specific syntax.
- A refusal from the safety patterns is policy, not a transient error. Do not retry the same intent with different phrasing; either work another way or tell the user why you stopped.
- Output beyond the cap is truncated head+tail, and the full text is written to a file whose path is in the result. Read that file rather than re-running the command.
- Set run_in_background=true for long-running processes (servers, watchers); a foreground command that exceeds its timeout is moved to the background rather than killed, and reported back when it finishes.

run_in_background.description: Run in background, return immediately with PID.

description.description: Brief description of what this command does.

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Fetch a URL and return its cleaned text content. Use this AFTER web_search to read the most promising result pages. Pass a 'prompt' describing what you need so the output is focused. Works on HTML pages, APIs, and plain text. Returns: url, status, content_type, bytes, duration_ms, result (cleaned text, wrapped in an <untrusted-content> delimiter).

prompt.description: What you are looking for on this page. Helps extract relevant content.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web. Uses Brave Search API if BRAVE_API_KEY is set, else DuckDuckGo HTML; auto-retries with a relaxed query on zero hits. Returns {results: [{title, url}], _meta: {backends_tried}}. IMPORTANT: After searching, pick the 1-3 most relevant URLs and use web_fetch to read their content. Do NOT keep searching endlessly — fetch the best results to extract the actual data. If the first search doesn't find what you need, try ONE more refined query, then fetch the best hits.

query.description: Search query. Be specific with names, dates, amounts.

allowed_domains.description: Only include results from these domains.

tools.name: edit_notebook_cell
tools.description: Edit or create a notebook cell by index.

tools.name: agent
tools.description: Launch a sub-agent with a scoped task. Optionally specify a role (research/work/validate) for automatic tool scoping, or provide explicit allowed_tools. By default this blocks until the sub-agent finishes (or times out after 5 minutes). Pass run_in_background=true for a long task to get a task_id back immediately instead of blocking — its result is delivered as a system-reminder on a later tool call, same as a background bash command.

run_in_background.description: Return immediately with a task_id instead of blocking (default false).

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Write or update the local todo list.

tools.name: mcp_list_resources
tools.description: List resources from a configured MCP server.

tools.name: mcp_read_resource
tools.description: Read a resource from a configured MCP server.

tools.name: load_skill
tools.description: Load a skill by name. Returns the full SKILL.md body.

tools.name: sleep
tools.description: Pause execution for the given number of milliseconds.

tools.name: config_read
tools.description: Read the current agent configuration.

tools.name: structured_output
tools.description: Return a structured JSON result.

tools.name: config_write
tools.description: Update a runtime configuration value.

tools.name: read_excel_sheet
tools.description: Read an Excel (.xlsx) sheet as headers + rows. Returns JSON with 'headers' and 'rows'.

tools.name: list_excel_sheets
tools.description: List visible sheet names in an Excel (.xlsx) file. Hidden sheets are excluded.

tools.name: inspect_excel_sheets
tools.description: Scan all visible sheets in an Excel file. Returns each sheet's name, estimated row count, column headers, and sample rows. Call this before read_excel_sheet when you need to identify which sheet contains the data the user is looking for.

sample_rows.description: Data rows to sample per sheet (default 3).

tools.name: write_excel_cell
tools.description: Write a value to a cell in an Excel (.xlsx) file.

tools.name: excel_to_json
tools.description: Convert an Excel sheet to a list of JSON records (using first row as headers).

tools.name: read_word_text
tools.description: Read the full text of a Word (.docx) file.

tools.name: read_word_paragraphs
tools.description: Read paragraphs from a Word (.docx) file with style info.

tools.name: write_word
tools.description: Create a new Word (.docx) file with paragraphs.

paragraphs.description: List of paragraphs. Each can be a string or {text, style}.

tools.name: append_word
tools.description: Append a paragraph to an existing Word (.docx) file.

tools.name: read_pptx
tools.description: Read text content from a PowerPoint (.pptx) file. Returns slide-by-slide text.

tools.name: write_pptx
tools.description: Create a new PowerPoint (.pptx) file with slides. Each slide has a title and body.

slides.description: List of slides. Each is {title, body} or {title, bullets: [...]}, plus optional 'notes' for the speaker notes and 'layout' for the slide-layout index (0 is the title slide in a stock template; default 1).

tools.name: write_pptx_from_template
tools.description: Create a PowerPoint (.pptx) from an existing template. Replaces placeholders in the template and adds slides with data.

slides.description: List of slides: each {title, body, bullets: [...], notes: str}.

tools.name: inspect_pptx_shapes
tools.description: Inspect a PowerPoint (.pptx) file's actual shape structure, per slide: each shape's name, type, position, and (for tables) row/column count with a cell preview, or (for text frames) a text preview. Call this before fill_pptx_shape_text/fill_pptx_table on a template whose shape names you don't already know — house-style templates typically name their content placeholders (e.g. a shape called 'textMainBullets' or 'Table Placeholder').

tools.name: fill_pptx_shape_text
tools.description: Write text into a specific named shape (text box or placeholder) on a specific slide of a .pptx file. Matches shape name case-insensitively. Use inspect_pptx_shapes first to find the right slide_index/shape_name. Pass the same path as output_path to keep progressively filling the same in-progress file. Applies the same fixed formatting estimate_pptx_text_capacity assumes (9pt Arial/Microsoft YaHei, single spacing, 3pt paragraph gap) so the two tools never disagree, and sets the shape's autofit accordingly: noAutofit when the text fits (exact size, no surprise PowerPoint shrink), or a bounded shrink-to-fit when it doesn't (visible, not silently clipped).

output_path.description: Path to save the result to.

paragraphs.description: List of paragraph strings; each becomes one paragraph/bullet.

is_chinese.description: Optional override for font selection; auto-detected (>30% CJK characters) if omitted.

tools.name: fill_pptx_table
tools.description: Write row data into a named table (or table placeholder) shape on a specific slide of a .pptx file. The target shape is always replaced with a freshly built table sized exactly to the given data, at the same position — this never silently crops data to an existing table's size. Optionally pass style_id to set a table style GUID. Matches shape name case-insensitively. Use inspect_pptx_shapes first to find slide_index/shape_name.

output_path.description: Path to save the result to.

rows.description: Row data: list of rows, each a list of cell strings.

style_id.description: Optional table style GUID (e.g. '{5C22544A-7EE6-4342-B048-85BDC9FD1C3A}') to apply.

tools.name: estimate_pptx_text_capacity
tools.description: Estimate whether commentary text fits a named shape's slot on a .pptx slide, using real font-glyph measurement (not a rough chars-per-inch guess). Pass the SAME paragraphs list you're about to write with fill_pptx_shape_text. Returns fill_ratio and remaining_lines_estimate -- use these to decide whether to add more genuinely-supported detail (a slot at fill_ratio 0.2-0.3 has room to spare) or trim (fill_ratio > 1.0 means it overflows). Call inspect_pptx_shapes first to find slide_index/shape_name.

paragraphs.description: Candidate paragraph strings, same shape as fill_pptx_shape_text's `paragraphs`.

is_chinese.description: Optional override; auto-detected (>30% CJK characters) if omitted.

tools.name: locate_databook_stage_columns
tools.description: Scan a financial databook sheet's header rows for reporting 'basis/stage' labels (Indicative adjusted, Mgt acc, Audited, Audit adjustment, Indicative adjustment -- including common Traditional/Simplified Chinese and typo variants) and return exactly which column each canonical stage occupies, with its associated period date. Call this BEFORE reading account figures from a databook, instead of visually picking which of many similarly-dated column groups is the required one (e.g. 'use only the Indicative adjusted columns') -- real databooks routinely place 10-30+ date columns side by side across 2-5 basis groups with only a text label distinguishing them, no cell merging or other structural hint. Returns found=false if the sheet doesn't have a recognizable multi-basis header.

max_scan_rows.description: Max rows to scan for the basis/header row (default 20).

tools.name: read_excel_preview
tools.description: Read an Excel file with schema inference. Returns headers, types, and a preview of the data.

tools.name: image_read
tools.description: Inspect an image (.png/.jpg/.jpeg/.webp/.gif/.bmp/.tiff) and return metadata (path, mime_type, width, height, mode, size_bytes). Pass include_base64=true to also get a base64 data URL — useful when the provider supports multimodal/vision input. Default omits base64 to keep the response cheap.

include_base64.description: If true, include a base64 data URL in the response.

tools.name: read_pdf_text
tools.description: Extract text from a PDF file. Returns page-by-page text. Pass layout=true to preserve the printed column positions with whitespace (pdftotext -layout equivalent) — use that mode when reading financial statements or any page where column alignment matters.

layout.description: Preserve printed column layout with whitespace (default false).

tools.name: extract_pdf_words
tools.description: All words on one PDF page with their x/y coordinates and x-centres. Low-level building block for coordinate-based table extraction when extract_pdf_period_table's automatic banding isn't enough (unusual layouts, matrix tables with text column headers).

tools.name: extract_pdf_period_table
tools.description: Column-safe extraction of a period-columned financial table from one PDF page. Detects the period headers (e.g. 2025 / 2024) by x-centre, builds a horizontal band per column, groups words into visual rows by y, and assigns each value to the period whose band its x-centre falls in — NEVER by token/reading order. Printed dashes count as 0 only inside a band; bracketed figures come back as real negatives; wrapped label lines are stitched onto their valued row; right-hand translated labels (bilingual statements) are kept separately and never counted as values. Use this for EVERY bilingual side-by-side note table. Returns found=false (with a reason) instead of guessing when the page has no text layer or no period header — flag those pages, do not invent columns.

periods.description: Expected period headers as printed (e.g. ["2025", "2024"]). Omit to auto-detect year-like headers.

tools.name: memory_save
tools.description: Persist a memory across sessions. Use for: user preferences, feedback corrections you should not repeat, project facts not derivable from code, references to external systems (Linear/Slack/Grafana). Do NOT save: code patterns derivable from the repo, ephemeral task state, anything already in CLAUDE.md/YUCODE.md/AGENTS.md.

description.description: One-line summary used to decide relevance in future sessions.

type.description: user = role/preferences; feedback = corrections to keep; project = ongoing work facts; reference = pointers to external systems.

content.description: The memory body. For feedback/project, structure as: rule/fact line, then a **Why:** line, then a **How to apply:** line.

tools.name: memory_list
tools.description: List saved memories with name, description, type, scope. Check this before saving a new memory to avoid duplicates.

scope.description: Optional scope filter; omit to list both.

tools.name: memory_read
tools.description: Read the full body of a saved memory by name. The MEMORY.md index in the prompt only shows descriptions; call this to see the actual content.

scope.description: Optional; searches workspace first, then user.

tools.name: memory_delete
tools.description: Delete a memory by name when it has turned out to be wrong, outdated, or no longer relevant.

tools.name: memory_search
tools.description: Full-text search across memory bodies for a keyword. Returns matching entries with name, description, scope.

tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description: Ask the user a question and wait for their answer. Use this only when the answer would change what you do next and you cannot determine it yourself from the workspace. Returns `cancelled: true` when there is no interactive terminal -- decide for yourself and state the assumption.

question.description: The question to put to the user.

options.description: Optional list of suggested answers, shown numbered.
